card.summary: Free premium link generator; the FAQ says 'Right now, you can to unrestrict almost 8 files per day.'

free_tier.stated: Free premium link generator; the FAQ says 'Right now, you can to unrestrict almost 8 files per day.'
free_tier.notes: 'almost 8' is the vendor's hedge, so the cap is soft.

per_object_cap.stated: 'We don't bother you with annoying file size limits.'
per_object_cap.notes: Stated only. The upstream host's own per-file cap still applies.

retention.stated: 'We will remove your premium link once you finish downloading the file.'

egress.terms: Served from OkDebrid's servers at '100% full download speed'. No byte allowance, no price.

record.interface_detail: Web form only: 'Enter your link', 'Get Premium Link', download. No API or CLI published.
record.chaining: Same slot as DebridHub: a zero-identity leecher for a few files a day. Eight files is below any real batch, so it is a spot tool.

limits.value: 'The generated premium link is locked and only accessible to the user that initiated the link generator'

record.limits_note: Claims to support 'about +100 cloud hosters' without publishing the list on the page read.
record.binding_note: The daily file count is the only stated ceiling. No byte figure exists to bind against.

identity_cost.detail: No registration. The generator runs against the caller's IP.

record.reliability_note: IP-locked links break on an egress change. The vendor advertises antivirus scanning of processed files, which is a scan of somebody else's file and not a guarantee about content.
record.confidence_note: Cap read on the vendor's FAQ. One completed download would raise it to measured.

evidence.proved: 'you can to unrestrict almost 8 files per day', the IP-locked link sentence, and the +100-host claim

record.notes: Copy matches DebridHub's page almost word for word, including the eight-links cap and the IP-lock sentence. Treat them as one product with two domains until someone compares their generated output.
